findings.summary: _Worker closes stdin and finish() then calls communicate(); on the production Python 3.12.14, communicate() raises ValueError('flush of closed file'), so every real worker result is rejected and no row is ever checkpointed.
findings.failure_scenario: Real v3 launch: worker 1 completes its match, then finish(1) calls worker.finish(), which raises. The row is marked record_unverified, stop is set, and all running rows fail the same way. The run stops with 0 rows persisted after the owner approval and claim were consumed, and no results branch exists, so a resume is impossible. Reproduced with the supervisor's own _Worker. Tests mock _launch with FakeWorker, so this path is untested.

findings.summary: The claim chain check is skipped when previous_claim.commit equals the publication, and _resume_target ties previous_claim to original_claim only for generation 1, so a rewound PR branch (reset to P or C0) passes for generation 2 and later.
findings.failure_scenario: The operator force-pushes the PR branch from C1 back to P (or C0) and builds a generation-2 request with previous_claim set to P (or C0). After the owner approves the digest, claim C2 is a child of P and all audits and worker rechecks pass while rows are reused. A fresh owner approval is still required.

findings.summary: Intermediate chain commits are only required to add one path under CLAIM_DIRECTORY (any name, subdirectory, mode or content), not a canonical consumption record.
findings.failure_scenario: A commit adding e.g. proxy-population-approval-consumption/notes/x.md between C0 and the previous claim is accepted as a 'claim' commit.

findings.summary: The saved per-row start.json (worker authorization evidence) is required but never parsed, hashed or bound. The checkpoint's original_claim/edition are copied from the descriptor, and the record is not replayed and the admission not re-checked.
findings.failure_scenario: A row pushed to fixed400-results/<id> with arbitrary start.json and a fabricated but self-consistent receipt/record (same bundle and tools hashes) is reused as reused_verified_checkpoint.

findings.summary: record_result swallows exceptions (including KeyboardInterrupt) on the success path without setting stop, so dispatch continues.
findings.failure_scenario: The result-NNNN.json write fails (ENOSPC or Ctrl-C) after a successful push. The row becomes record_unverified, the supervisor keeps launching the remaining schedule, and the interrupt is raised only at the end. The old supervisor stopped.

findings.summary: A dispatch failure of a later row sets stop, so lower-index running rows that then complete are discarded as completed_not_saved. An interrupt caught inside finish() does not terminate sibling workers.
findings.failure_scenario: dispatch(4) hits an OSError, and rows 1-3 that complete afterwards are not checkpointed. A Ctrl-C during git push in finish() leaves 3 workers running about 20 minutes before the stop.

findings.summary: Worker stdout/stderr pipes are not drained until finish(), and only the lowest worker is polled.
findings.failure_scenario: The lowest worker writes more than 64 KiB to stderr (a long traceback or audit-error text), blocks on write and never exits, so the supervisor hangs with no stop record. The old supervisor used subprocess.run, which drains the pipes.

findings.summary: unsaved_completed_rows counts only persist_failed, not completed_not_saved.
findings.failure_scenario: Parallelism 4: row 1 incomplete, rows 2-4 completed but unsaved, and the report says unsaved_completed_rows=0.

findings.summary: An interruption before the first successful push leaves no results branch. prepare_resume refuses, and generation 1 and later requires results_ref. Prevalidate/consume also do not re-verify the results ref before consuming the comment.
findings.failure_scenario: The container is lost during row 1, and no contract path to resume exists (generation 0 needs PR head == P) without manually pushing C0 as the results branch. If the results branch moves after the request was built, the approval is consumed and the supervisor then stops.

findings.summary: A same-container resume fails: the fixed workspace name results-<attempt> must not exist, and checkout -B of a branch checked out in the old worktree is refused on git 2.44 and later. A workspace under docs/card-game breaks edition rglob('*.py').
findings.failure_scenario: A same-container resume with the same store_workspace raises 'results workspace already exists' after consumption. A workspace placed under docs/card-game makes every edition.verify fail.

findings.summary: active_cards no longer digests single-generation cards, so a non-canonical card value no longer raises.
findings.failure_scenario: cards={'A-001#1':{...,'cost':1.5}}: the old code raises ValueError('unsupported JSON type'), and the new code returns {'A-001':'A-001#1'} (reproduced). Unreachable for canonical, manifest-derived states.

findings.summary: On a catalog() cache hit, the fixture hash and source-section checks are skipped.
findings.failure_scenario: The fixture-107 JSON or a referenced rules .md changes after the first call in a worker: the old code raised 'start source text changed', and the new code returns the cached catalog. Only a transient change escapes the edition verify around each match.
